Claim: Human clinical platelet risk is not a nucleotide-sequence-only property.
Permitted_Wording: Within two matched nucleotide-sequence families, different conjugation and exposure contexts were associated with different platelet-risk profiles; sequence, chemistry, dose, frequency, exposure, population, and monitoring must remain explicit.
Prohibited_Wording: GalNAc alone prevents thrombocytopenia; the shared sequence is intrinsically safe or intrinsically toxic.

Claim: Volanesorsen produced frequent clinically important platelet reductions in the APPROACH trial, including two very severe nadirs.
Permitted_Wording: Volanesorsen was associated with frequent platelet reductions; two treated participants had counts below 25,000/µL, and no placebo participant had a count below 100,000/µL.
Prohibited_Wording: Every exposed patient develops thrombocytopenia; the mechanism is proven to be sequence-specific.

Claim: Inotersen has documented rare severe thrombocytopenia with platelet-reactive IgG and a fatal hemorrhagic event.
Evidence_Level: Randomized human clinical plus case-level mechanistic evidence
Permitted_Wording: Rare severe inotersen-associated cases included platelet-reactive IgG; one severe event was associated with fatal intracranial hemorrhage.
Prohibited_Wording: All inotersen platelet declines are immune mediated; platelet antibodies predict all cases.

Claim: Moderate phenotype-1 platelet decline is distinct from rare severe phenotype-2 thrombocytopenia.
Evidence_Objects: Clinical_Endpoint_Ontology; Slingsby 2022; Crooke pooled clinical tables
Permitted_Wording: The dataset separates a moderate, often dose-related and reversible platelet-count decline from rare severe cases with possible immune features.
Prohibited_Wording: Phenotype 1 and phenotype 2 are the same biological process or can be modeled with one unqualified binary endpoint.

Claim: Selected phosphorothioate ASOs activate human platelets in a sequence-dependent manner under defined ex vivo conditions.
Permitted_Wording: The five-ASO Slingsby panel showed sequence-dependent differences in human platelet activation and platelet-leukocyte aggregate formation under the reported assay conditions.
Prohibited_Wording: The assay proves clinical thrombocytopenia risk for all ASOs.

Claim: GPVI is a supported platelet-interaction pathway for the tested ASOs.
Evidence_Objects: Slingsby GPVI binding/activation rows; Sewing matched constructs
Evidence_Level: Primary human protein and platelet mechanistic
Permitted_Wording: GPVI binding and GPVI/SYK-associated activation are supported for the tested ASOs and donors.
Prohibited_Wording: GPVI explains every clinical platelet decline or every ASO chemistry.

Claim: Changing ODN2395 from PS to PO backbone removed the strong response in the matched assay.
Permitted_Wording: In the ODN2395 matched construct pair, the PS version showed strong activation whereas the PO version showed no/low detected activation.
Prohibited_Wording: All PS oligonucleotides activate platelets and all PO oligonucleotides are safe.

Claim: LNA wings reduced activation in the three matched alternating-AC constructs tested by Sewing et al.
Permitted_Wording: For AC8, AC9, and AC10 under the reported conditions, adding LNA wings was associated with lower GPVI/PF4 binding and platelet activation.
Prohibited_Wording: LNA universally prevents thrombocytopenia or platelet activation.

Claim: The tested Slingsby ASOs did not suppress human megakaryocyte proplatelet production.
Permitted_Wording: None of the five tested ASOs inhibited proplatelet production in the reported human cord-blood-derived megakaryocyte system.
Prohibited_Wording: ASOs cannot affect platelet production in humans.

Claim: Human ex vivo platelet activation is not equivalent to clinical thrombocytopenia.
Permitted_Wording: Ex vivo platelet interaction is a mechanistic endpoint that may inform hypotheses but must remain separate from direct human platelet-count outcomes.
Prohibited_Wording: A positive ex vivo activation assay is a clinical thrombocytopenia label.

Claim: Olezarsen and eplontersen are lower-risk context comparators, not clean sequence-linked clinical negatives.
Permitted_Wording: The GalNAc-conjugated derivatives provide informative lower-risk treatment-context comparisons but still have reported platelet-related observations or non-equivalent designs.
Prohibited_Wording: Olezarsen and eplontersen are proven thrombocytopenia-negative controls.

Claim: The present corpus contains zero clean sequence-linked clinical negatives that satisfy all adjudication gates.
Permitted_Wording: No current candidate simultaneously satisfies exact sequence linkage, adequate human exposure, explicit platelet monitoring, sufficient dose/duration, reported platelet outcome, and recoverable provenance.
Prohibited_Wording: There are no clinically safe oligonucleotides; absence of a clean negative proves universal risk.
Source_URL: Internal v0.9 scientist audit; source URLs retained per candidate

Claim: A conventional sequence-only clinical thrombocytopenia classifier is not currently scientifically supportable.
Permitted_Wording: The available human clinical evidence supports descriptive, matched-context, and case-series analyses, but not a balanced sequence-only classifier.
Prohibited_Wording: A clinical sequence model has been validated or has meaningful AUC.

Claim: Analytical identity and purity remain unreported for all 45 current oligo/product records in the available corpus.
Permitted_Wording: Sequence and position-level chemistry have been reconstructed, but this is not equivalent to analytical identity, purity, observed molecular weight, or lot characterization.
Prohibited_Wording: All oligos are analytically characterized or meet a common purity specification.

Claim: SafeSense is a high-value expansion source but its records require treatment-context adjudication.
Permitted_Wording: SafeSense aggregates human safety information across 112 ASOs and provides a valuable expansion source; its heterogeneous treatment records must retain dose, route, indication, comparator, and provenance limitations.
Prohibited_Wording: Every SafeSense adverse-event row is a causal or sequence-level toxicity label.
Confidence: HIGH FOR RESOURCE SCOPE; VARIABLE FOR INDIVIDUAL ROWS
Scientific_Status: APPROVED AS EXPANSION SOURCE, NOT AUTO-LABEL SOURCE

Claim: The Phase 2 product is an auditable AI-ready derivative dataset, not a set of literature summaries.
Permitted_Wording: Each eligible row is linked to an oligo construct, position-resolved chemistry, experimental or clinical context, endpoint, scientific adjudication, and source provenance.
Prohibited_Wording: The dataset is final, fully characterized, or ready for unrestricted clinical prediction.
